text:
alana: Heads-up: after the NF4 calibration sweep deployed to dedicated-pool-2, we've seen ~18% throughput drop and a GPU memory spike on 4096-context runs. Can eng-runtime triage?

ravi: ugh. saw a perf alert too. perf-bot posted a spike at 1769123460. Any idea which kernel is being chosen?

alana: looks like q4_kern_v2 is being selected but the fallback path to q4_fallback_fp4_kern ends up being used for many sequences — weird selector behaviour.

jun: do we have profiling traces from the failing hosts? can someone paste the nvprof / tracy snippet?

alana: attaching quick slice (logs trimmed):

```
[1769123462] host-12 - model: redwood-ggml-nf4
gpu_mem: 14372 MiB -> 19234 MiB within 30s
kernel_select: q4_kern_v2 -> q4_fallback_fp4_kern
throughput: 420 tok/s -> 340 tok/s
batch_size distribution: [1: 62%, 2: 28%, 4+: 10%]
KV_cache growth: per-request +1.8MB avg
```

olivia: that KV cache growth looks suspicious — is calibration storing extra cached prefixes or increasing key precision?

mike: quick note — the calibration sweep changed dynamic range scaling for NF4 (shifted calibration shard to use per-layer minmax instead of global). That can change dequantization mem usage and also trigger different kernel paths if heuristics rely on quant params.

ravi: ok that explains memory. Why throughput drop though? q4_fallback_fp4_kern is less optimized for continuous batching; it disables the fused attention kernel we use for q4_kern_v2. More kernel launches -> latency per token up.

alana: can we force kernel selection to prefer q4_kern_v2 for a canary group and see if perf restores? We should also compare calibration outputs between previous and new calibration for layer 12..24.

jun: running an A/B canary now on host-12 and host-13 with ENV override KERN_PREF=prefer_q4_v2 and CALIB_BACKOFF=1. Will report in ~10m.

perf-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool-2 average p50 latency for redwood-ggml-nf4 increased from 120ms to 220ms at 1769123471.

mike: if forced kernel fixes throughput, we need to update kernel selection rules to include calibration-derived flags (e.g., per-layer-dtype-hint) to avoid auto-fallback when memory spike is due to calibration artifacts.

olivia: also check batching heuristics: we're seeing many single-item batches. Calibration may be increasing CPU preproc time causing requests to miss batching windows. Check ttfb distribution.

alana: good catch — ttfb p95 jumped from 15ms to 90ms on those hosts. Could be CPU-side quant dequant overhead.

ravi: action items: 1) Jun to finish canary and paste prometheus + nvprof traces; 2) Mike to run a mini calibration revert on a staging copy and diff per-layer ranges; 3) Olivia to run batching simulator with new per-request ttfb to see SLO impact; 4) Alana to prepare rollback plan if canary fails.

jun: canary update: forcing q4_kern_v2 restored throughput to ~410 tok/s and memory stayed near baseline. nvprof shows fused attention runs again. Uploading traces to /tmp/nf4_canary_traces.tar.gz (link: https://internal/artifacts/nf4_canary_traces.tar.gz)

alana: awesome — sounds like immediate mitigation is kernel-preference until we fix calibration. I'll draft a rollback/canary policy for Dedicated.

mike: follow-up — we should add a calibration step to the release checklist that runs a perf microbenchmark (batching + KV growth) so future calibration changes don't regress runtime heuristics.

olivia: agree. also add an alert that correlates sudden KV_cache growth with kernel fallback events. That would have caught this earlier.

alana: thanks team. I'll file a short postmortem and tag infra and ml-calib. For now I'll pin the canary override on the affected nodes. :thumbsup:
